title:
The framework that
works at big pharma
*breaks* at mid-size.
sub: It's almost never the framework. It's what people carry in with them.

title: I've worked all three sizes.
text:
15 years in big pharma. Four in mid-size. Then startups. Then back again.

Same regulations every time. Completely different physics.

title: Small and mid-size companies hire *from* big pharma.
text: They get the experience they paid for. They also get the mentality that came with it — and nobody mentions that part in the interview.

title:
Their first GxP system —
and the date mattered.
text:
A statistical computing platform (SAS). Six months, limited scope, roughly 75% out-of-the-box vendor features — with vendor qualification documentation for all of it.

Regulatory submission preparation was waiting on the go-live.
tag: First GxP system. No local precedent.

title: Two months late.
text:
QA asked the CSV team to fully validate the out-of-the-box features — the way you would with a hundred-person validation function and no deadline. The vendor's own evidence sat there, unused.

Submission prep slipped. So did every system downstream.

title: The part nobody says out loud:
text:
Over-validation is billable. Under-validation isn't.

That asymmetry shapes more decisions than anyone admits — and the company carrying the delay is never the one being paid for it.

title: This wasn't a *framework* gap.
text:
Risk-based validation was right there in the SOP. CSA was available. Vendor evidence was leverageable.

But it was their first GxP system — no local precedent, nothing to push back against the imported default: validate everything.

title:
What to unlearn when
you move down a size:
items: *We have a team for that* → you are the team
*The SOP will tell us* → you will write the SOP
*Vendor docs aren't enough* → often they're exactly enough
*A six-week workshop* → a decision, in a room, this afternoon

title:
What actually made me useful
wasn't the CSV knowledge.
text:
It was leadership, teaching, negotiation, workshop facilitation, communicating risk to people who don't want to hear it.

The technical part is table stakes. Getting a room of experienced people to change how they work is the job.

title:
Has your org started the
AI-in-GxP journey?
text:
Forward this to your QA, CSV or IT lead — especially if your team was built by hiring from bigger companies.
